ev.k5_herd_stray.title: The stray
ev.k5_herd_stray.text: For the first time you were trusted to herd the goats alone. By evening you count them - one is missing. The white one with the torn ear is standing on a ledge above the ravine, chewing a bush with perfect calm.
ev.k5_herd_stray.climb: Climb up the rocks after her
ev.k5_herd_stray.climb.success: You reached the rope around her neck and led the stubborn thing down. At home they called you a herder for the first time - and nobody laughed.
ev.k5_herd_stray.climb.failure: A stone slid from under your foot and you skidded into the ravine, skinning both knees. The goat came down on her own - right behind you, looking curious.
ev.k5_herd_stray.salt: Lure her with salt on your palm
ev.k5_herd_stray.salt.success: The goat smelled the salt, came down and followed you as if on a lead. The old herder grunted: he had invented that trick himself some forty years ago.
ev.k5_herd_stray.salt.failure: The goat licked up the salt, gave you a grateful look and climbed even higher. A neighbor had to fetch her down, and he had to be paid for his trouble.
ev.k5_gleaning.title: Gleaning
ev.k5_gleaning.text: After the harvest, children walk the reaped field picking up the ears left behind - that is how the poor have always eaten. But at the edge of the field stand untouched sheaves, and the watchman has dozed off under a tree.
ev.k5_gleaning.text.MAY: After the harvest, children walk through someone else's field picking up the missed cobs - that is how the poor have always eaten. But at the edge of the field lies a heap of unhusked cobs, and the watchman has dozed off in the shade.
ev.k5_gleaning.text.AMR: After the harvest, children walk through someone else's field picking up the missed cobs - that is how the poor have always eaten. But at the edge of the field lies a heap of unhusked cobs, and the watchman has dozed off in the shade.
ev.k5_gleaning.ground: Pick only from the ground, as is proper
ev.k5_gleaning.pinch: Help yourself under the watchman's nose
ev.k5_gleaning.pinch.success: The watchman never woke. At home your haul became a thick stew, and nobody asked where so much had come from.
ev.k5_gleaning.pinch.failure: The watchman woke at the worst possible moment. He chased you across the whole field, and by evening the whole district knew of your disgrace.
ev.k5_gleaning.share: Give your handful to the old woman gleaning beside you
ev.k5_water_jar.title: The broken jar
ev.k5_water_jar.text: You are carrying water in a big jar - the third trip this morning. Halfway home the handle slips from your wet fingers and the jar shatters on a stone. The water vanishes into the dust before you can even gasp.
ev.k5_water_jar.text.RUS: You are carrying water on a yoke - the third trip this morning. Halfway home you slip, a bucket bangs on a stone and its bottom flies out. The water soaks into the ground before you can even gasp.
ev.k5_water_jar.text.CHN: You are carrying water on a shoulder pole - the third trip this morning. Halfway home you slip, a bucket bangs on a stone and splits. The water soaks into the ground before you can even gasp.
ev.k5_water_jar.text.JPN: You are carrying water on a shoulder pole - the third trip this morning. Halfway home you slip, a bucket bangs on a stone and splits. The water soaks into the ground before you can even gasp.
ev.k5_water_jar.hide: Hide the pieces and act as if nothing happened
ev.k5_water_jar.hide.success: Nobody noticed it was gone for a week, and then they decided some stranger had walked off with it. You still feel a little ashamed.
ev.k5_water_jar.hide.failure: The neighbors' dog dug up the pieces and proudly dragged them to the doorstep. You caught it for the breakage, and even more for the lie.
ev.k5_water_jar.carry: Carry water in whatever comes to hand until you've brought enough
ev.k5_field_talent.title: A sharp memory
ev.k5_field_talent.text: You remember everything: how much grain the neighbors borrowed, the day the rains came, whose goats trampled the boundary strip. The village headman heard you correct the grown-ups in an argument and grew thoughtful. He knows a man who teaches signs and reckoning - but there you have to sit, not work the fields.
ev.k5_field_talent.learn: Beg to be let go to study
ev.k5_field_talent.field: Stay in the field: hands are needed more
ev.k5_field_talent.evenings: Study in snatches, in the evenings
ev.k5_field_talent.evenings.success: You fell asleep over the signs, but by winter you could reckon faster than the headman. He pretended not to notice.
ev.k5_field_talent.evenings.failure: Fields by day, lessons by night - within a month you nodded off in the middle of an explanation. The teacher sighed: everything in its own time.
ev.k5_f_village_reader.title: The district's reader
ev.k5_f_village_reader.text: You are nearly the only one in the district who can read signs and reckon without pebbles. People bring you everything: debt records, news from afar, boundary disputes. Today the tax collector has arrived, and the neighbors are looking at you hopefully.
ev.k5_f_village_reader.check: Check his sums in front of everyone
ev.k5_f_village_reader.check.success: You found an extra measure charged to every household. The collector turned purple, but he recounted. That evening the neighbors brought you whatever they could spare.
ev.k5_f_village_reader.check.failure: There was no mistake - his sums were right. The collector left, but he remembered your face, and next time your household was taxed down to the last grain.
ev.k5_f_village_reader.quiet: Explain it to the neighbors later, quietly
ev.k5_night_watch.title: Night watch
ev.k5_night_watch.text: The crop is nearly ripe, and at night animals come out to the field. You've been put in a hut at the field's edge to keep watch until dawn. It's dark, something rustles in the thicket, and your eyes keep closing.
ev.k5_night_watch.awake: Stay awake: sing, pinch yourself, count stars
ev.k5_night_watch.awake.success: Near dawn an animal stepped out of the thicket, and you shrieked so loud it bolted, flattening a fence on its way. The field is safe, and you are the hero of the morning.
ev.k5_night_watch.awake.failure: You held out until the last star and fell asleep a moment before dawn. In the morning there were tracks at the field's edge and chewed stalks.
ev.k5_night_watch.noise: Bang a stick on a pot all night long
ev.k5_night_watch.nap: Sleep a little - animals sleep too, surely
ev.k5_night_watch.nap.success: You slept till dawn and nothing happened. The grown-ups praised you for being so watchful, and you modestly said nothing.
ev.k5_night_watch.nap.failure: Animals, it turns out, don't sleep. By morning half a strip had been trampled, and you woke to the grown-ups shouting.
ev.k5_ruined_work.title: The crack
ev.k5_ruined_work.text: For the first time the workshop trusted you with real work - finishing a piece a customer is already waiting for. You tried so hard that you pressed too firmly, and a crack ran across it. The master will be back by evening.
ev.k5_ruined_work.confess: Wait for the master and show him
ev.k5_ruined_work.hide: Hide it in the pile of spoiled work
ev.k5_ruined_work.hide.success: The master only went through the spoiled pile a month later and decided it had cracked by itself. For a long time you couldn't meet his eyes.
ev.k5_ruined_work.hide.failure: The master found it that very evening - he always checks the spoiled pile first. The punishment was short; the silence afterwards was long.
ev.k5_ruined_work.redo: Try to make it again while no one's here
ev.k5_ruined_work.redo.success: When the master returned, a new piece stood in its place - a bit lopsided, but whole. He turned it over in his hands, said nothing for a while, then: 'Tomorrow you'll make another.'
ev.k5_ruined_work.redo.failure: The second came out worse than the first, the third worse than the second. The master found you among the fragments and didn't even scold - he just counted the waste.
ev.k5_journeyman_trick.title: The journeyman's trick
ev.k5_journeyman_trick.text: The journeyman who has worked in the shop for three years took you aside and showed you a trick: how to do in one movement what takes the master half a day. 'Not a word to anyone,' he whispers. 'The master says it ruins the craft.'
ev.k5_journeyman_trick.try.success: It worked the first time! The journeyman whistled: it had taken him a week.
ev.k5_journeyman_trick.try.failure: The trick needed experience as well as the movement. The master found the ruined piece, and the journeyman acted as if he'd never seen you before.
ev.k5_f_trick_pays.title: The old trick
ev.k5_f_trick_pays.text: An order is due: a week's work and two days to do it. Then you remember the trick a journeyman showed you as a child. It would go three times faster, but the old masters would call it botching.
ev.k5_f_trick_pays.quick.success: The customer got his work on time and noticed nothing but how fast you were. A month later he brought two more.
ev.k5_f_trick_pays.quick.failure: The trick let you down: within a month the piece began to come apart. The customer came back - and has talked about you on every corner since.
ev.k5_f_trick_pays.old_way: Work the old way, through the nights
ev.k5_first_tip.title: First earnings
ev.k5_first_tip.text: You were sent to carry a heavy basket to a rich house. The lady of the house looked it all over, was pleased, and pressed a small payment into your palm - not for the basket, but for you, for your quick legs. The first thing you ever earned yourself.
ev.k5_first_tip.stash: Hide it in your secret place
ev.k5_first_tip.treat: Buy sweets for your whole gang of friends
ev.k5_count_for_father.title: Counting pebbles
ev.k5_count_for_father.text: {npc}, your father, has let you keep count for the first time: for every measure sold you set aside a pebble while he haggles. Toward evening you notice he gave one old man less than he paid for. Whether by mistake or not, you can't tell.
ev.k5_count_for_father.tell_father.succe: He reddened, recounted, ran after the old man and made up the difference. That evening he said you keep count better than many a clerk.
ev.k5_count_for_father.tell_father.failu: Your father frowned: 'Count your pebbles and stay out of what isn't yours.' You counted in silence until evening.
ev.k5_count_for_father.tell_buyer: Run after the old man and tell him
ev.k5_f_honest_child.text: The old man you once chased across the market died long ago, but a kinsman of his tracked you down: to the end of his days the old man told of the honest child at the stall. The kinsman now runs a large business and wants to do it with you.
ev.k5_market_stranger.title: A light bundle
ev.k5_market_stranger.text: You've been sent across the market on an errand. On the way a stranger calls out: take this bundle to the gate, someone's waiting, and you'll be paid twice the usual. The bundle is suspiciously light, and the stranger keeps glancing over his shoulder.
ev.k5_market_stranger.errand: Don't stop: your own errand comes first
ev.k5_market_stranger.carry: Take the bundle - the pay is good
ev.k5_market_stranger.carry.success: At the gate a man silently took the bundle and paid you. What was inside you never found out - which was probably for the best.
ev.k5_market_stranger.carry.failure: At the gate the bundle was awaited not by the stranger's friends but by the people chasing him. You barely managed to explain you had nothing to do with it, but the market looked at you sideways for a long time.
ev.k5_market_stranger.report: Point the stranger out to the market warden
ev.k5_market_stranger.report.success: The warden recognized the thief they'd been hunting since morning. You were praised before the whole market and given a double handful of dried fruit.
ev.k5_market_stranger.report.failure: While you looked for the warden, the stranger melted into the crowd. The warden heard you out and advised you to make up fewer stories.
ev.k5_haggle_alone.title: Alone at the stall
ev.k5_haggle_alone.text: The grown-ups have stepped away, and for the first time you're minding the stall alone. Up comes a customer - the kind who haggles for the fun of it. She picks the very best and offers half the price.
ev.k5_haggle_alone.hold.success: You argued until the sun had moved a hand's width. She paid your price and, leaving, told the neighbors: 'That child knows what's what.'
ev.k5_haggle_alone.hold.failure: The customer sniffed and went to the next stall, where they gave way. It stings, but you held your price.
ev.k5_haggle_alone.yield: Give in - as long as she buys
ev.k5_haggle_alone.gift: Keep the price but throw in a little something
ev.k5_haggle_alone.gift.success: The little gift won her over and she paid in full. Three days later she came back - and brought a friend.
ev.k5_haggle_alone.gift.failure: She took the gift with pleasure and then knocked off a third anyway. From people like her you could learn haggling for years.
ev.k5_strict_tutor.title: The strict tutor
ev.k5_strict_tutor.text: You've been given a tutor - a dry man who never smiles and forgives no mistake. For an error he raps your fingers with a stick; for an unlearned lesson you go without your meal. Today, again, you haven't learned the lesson, and the sun is shining outside.
ev.k5_strict_tutor.endure: Sit and study until you've got it
ev.k5_strict_tutor.prank.success: The tutor spent half the day looking for his stick and finally taught without it. Strangely, it was the most peaceful lesson in a month.
ev.k5_strict_tutor.prank.failure: He found the stick in no time - by your guilty face. That day the lesson lasted until dark.
ev.k5_strict_tutor.complain: Complain to the elders of the house
ev.k5_strict_tutor.complain.success: Nobody knows what was said to him, but from then on the tutor struck less often, and once he even nodded: 'Not bad.'
ev.k5_strict_tutor.complain.failure: The elders listened and decided the tutor is always right. The tutor heard about it too - and remembered.
ev.k5_f_old_tutor.title: The old tutor
ev.k5_f_old_tutor.text: An old man in shabby clothes stands at the door, and it takes you a moment to recognize your strict tutor. His pupils have scattered, his strength is gone, and he is plainly not used to asking. All he says is: 'You were one of the few who learned their lessons.'
ev.k5_f_old_tutor.take_in: Take him in - let him teach the young ones
ev.k5_f_old_tutor.alms: Give him something for the road
ev.k5_tenant_tally.title: The shortfall
ev.k5_tenant_tally.text: The steward has taken you along to collect the harvest share from those who work your land - time to learn the estate. One household's share comes up short: half their field rotted, and there's a sick old man in the house. The steward nods to you: 'Write down what's missing - we'll collect it by spring.'
ev.k5_tenant_tally.write: Write it down as it is
ev.k5_tenant_tally.forgive: Write down the full share, as if all was paid
ev.k5_tenant_tally.forgive.success: The steward didn't recount. A week later someone left a basket of the best fruit at the gate - without a word.
ev.k5_tenant_tally.forgive.failure: The steward recounted the sacks and silently corrected the record. On the way back he said: 'Kindness at someone else's expense isn't kindness.'
ev.k5_tenant_tally.ask: Ask the steward for a delay
ev.k5_tenant_tally.ask.success: The steward scratched his head and agreed: there's nothing to take from a sick house anyway. The family bowed to you all the way to the gate.
ev.k5_tenant_tally.ask.failure: 'The master decides, not you,' the steward snapped. Though there was something like respect in his voice.
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.title: One good turn
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.text: At night a young man knocks at the gate - you recognize the boy from that very household you once helped with their shortfall. He whispers: beyond the hill a band of rough men is gathering, and they're talking about your house.
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.stand: Rouse your people and meet them at the gate
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.stand.success: The raiders found the gate barred and a dozen people with cudgels behind it. They left without starting. By morning the whole district was talking about how well you'd managed.
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.stand.failure: It was a terrible night: the gate held, but the storeroom was plundered, and you were hurt in the scuffle.
ev.k5_f_tenant_son.hide: Hide the most valuable things and leave until morning
ev.k5_judgment_seat.title: Beside the elders
ev.k5_judgment_seat.text: For the first time you've been seated beside the elders as they hear complaints. You must sit straight, keep quiet and learn. Before you a poor widow weeps: her neighbor moved the boundary stones and ploughed her strip, and he swears the stones have always stood there.
ev.k5_judgment_seat.silent: Sit in silence, as you were told
ev.k5_judgment_seat.speak: Whisper to the elders that last spring the stones stood elsewhere
ev.k5_judgment_seat.speak.success: The elders exchanged looks and sent someone to check. Under the stones the earth was fresh. The widow got her strip back, and for the first time they nodded to you as to a grown-up.
ev.k5_judgment_seat.speak.failure: The look you got made you shrink. Afterwards it was explained to you: here one speaks when spoken to.
ev.k5_judgment_seat.doze: Doze off - the hearing has dragged on for three hours
ev.k5_judgment_seat.doze.success: You woke at the thud of a staff on the floor - the judgment was already given. Nobody noticed anything, except the widow, who smiled at you as she left.
ev.k5_judgment_seat.doze.failure: You snored loudly through the whole hall at the most solemn moment. The defendant burst out laughing, and the hearing had to be halted.
ev.k5_etiquette.title: Greeting the guest
ev.k5_etiquette.text: An important guest has arrived, and you've been brought out to greet him. You spent a week learning the words: the bow, the form of address, all his titles in order. And now you stand before him - and your head is as empty as a swept room.
ev.k5_etiquette.improvise: Say something in your own words, but boldly
ev.k5_etiquette.improvise.success: You said you were gladder of him than of a feast day, and that his titles were so long they had to be learned from dawn. The guest roared with laughter and gave you his ring.
ev.k5_etiquette.improvise.failure: You began briskly, mixed up the titles and finished with the words one uses to greet a cook. The guest smiled politely. The elders did not.
ev.k5_etiquette.bow: Bow as low as you can, in silence
ev.k5_etiquette.prompt: Glance at the old servant - he's whispering prompts
ev.k5_etiquette.prompt.success: The servant whispered, you repeated word for word, and it came out flawless. The guest praised your memory, and you and the servant traded looks like conspirators.
ev.k5_etiquette.prompt.failure: You didn't quite catch the whisper and addressed the guest by the title of his old rival. The hall went very quiet.
ev.k5_whispered_answers.title: Whispers in class
ev.k5_whispered_answers.text: So you wouldn't be bored at lessons, a servant {g:boy|girl} was seated beside you. The tutor never asks {g:him|her} anything, but {g:he|she} picks things up faster than you and whispers the answers. Today the tutor heard the whisper and is asking whose voice it was.
ev.k5_whispered_answers.admit: Own up: the whispers were for you
ev.k5_whispered_answers.both: Ask the tutor to teach you both
ev.k5_whispered_answers.both.success: The tutor snorted but agreed - anything to make you study more willingly. From then on you sat side by side openly, and you tried your hardest to keep up.
ev.k5_whispered_answers.both.failure: The tutor replied that letters are not for servants, and {g:he|she} was moved to a seat by the door. There's no one left to whisper.
ev.k5_f_companion.text: The one who used to whisper answers to you in lessons grew up long ago and now runs the household of a great house. Word came: if you ever need a trustworthy person who can read and write - they remember who once stood up for them.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.title: A piece from a guest's plate
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.text: You stand by the wall while the master's guests eat. One of them, fat and jolly, quietly beckoned you over and held out a piece from his own plate. Slaves are forbidden to take food from the guests' table, and the steward is looking the other way - for now.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.save: Take it and hide it for the little ones in the kitchen
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.save.success: That evening in the kitchen the piece was split five ways, and everyone made their share last as long as they could. The old cook said you have a kind heart and a reckless head.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.save.failure: The steward noticed you hiding something in your clothes. The piece was taken away and you were punished - briefly, but it hurt.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.eat: Eat it at once, while no one's looking
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.eat.success: You swallowed it almost without chewing. You'd never tasted anything so good in your life, and the guest winked at you as he left.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.eat.failure: You choked right there by the wall, and everyone turned. The guest was embarrassed, but it was you who got punished.
ev.k5_slave_leftovers.refuse: Shake your head and lower your eyes
ev.k5_slave_storeroom.title: Lessons in the storeroom
ev.k5_slave_storeroom.text: The old slave who keeps the storeroom has noticed how quickly you count. He offers to teach you in the evenings to keep account of the stores - with notches and marks, the way he knows how. The master never ordered this, and if you're caught idling in the storeroom, you'll both be in trouble.
ev.k5_slave_storeroom.learn.success: All winter you counted sacks and jars by a smoky little lamp. In spring the old man said you count better than he does, and for the first time you can remember, he smiled.
ev.k5_slave_storeroom.learn.failure: You were caught on the third evening. The old man got it worse than you, but he didn't stop teaching - he just grew more careful.
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.title: The storeroom keys
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.text: The old storekeeper has died, and the master is looking for someone to trust with the keys. Someone remembered that the old man taught you to count. The keys mean better food, a corner of your own and respect - but also answering for every missing measure.
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.feed: Take the keys and quietly feed your own people
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.feed.success: You learned to keep the accounts so that an extra handful for the hungry shows up in no record at all. The old man would have been proud of you.
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.feed.failure: The shortfall was spotted at the very first recount. The keys were taken from you, and the punishment was harsh.
ev.k5_f_storeroom_keys.decline: Refuse: too much to answer for
ev.k5_slave_errand.title: The storyteller in the square
ev.k5_slave_errand.text: You were sent across the whole city on an errand, and on the way back you came upon a square where a storyteller had gathered a crowd. He has just reached the most frightening part. You're expected back by noon, and the sun is already high.
ev.k5_slave_errand.listen: Hear at least this story to the end
ev.k5_slave_errand.listen.success: You heard it to the end and ran so fast the dust stood up in a column. Nobody noticed you were late, and you retold the story in the kitchen for a week.
ev.k5_slave_errand.listen.failure: You got back when the shadows were long. The steward didn't care to hear where you'd been - and the punishment lasted longer than the story.
ev.k5_slave_errand.backwards: Listen on the move, backing toward the lane
ev.k5_slave_errand.backwards.success: You backed away so slowly that you heard nearly everything and still made it by noon. You made up the ending yourself - and it was better.
ev.k5_slave_errand.backwards.failure: Backing away, you crashed into a market woman's basket, and instead of the ending you heard everything she thought of you.
ev.k5_ink_spill.title: The blot
ev.k5_ink_spill.text: The teacher stepped out for a minute, leaving his best work on the table - the one he spent half a year copying. You leaned in for a closer look and knocked over the ink. A black stain is spreading across the lines.
ev.k5_ink_spill.text.babylon: The teacher stepped out for a minute, leaving a fresh clay tablet on the table - the one he's been working on since morning. You leaned in for a closer look and your sleeve smeared half the signs. The clay is still soft, but what was written can no longer be read.
ev.k5_ink_spill.text.assur: The teacher stepped out for a minute, leaving a fresh clay tablet on the table - the one he's been working on since morning. You leaned in for a closer look and your sleeve smeared half the signs. The clay is still soft, but what was written can no longer be read.
ev.k5_ink_spill.confess: Wait for the teacher and confess
ev.k5_ink_spill.redo: Try to restore the damage yourself
ev.k5_ink_spill.redo.success: You sat till dark, tracing sign after sign. The teacher looked at your work for a long time, then said: 'Your hand is dreadful. Come early tomorrow - I'll train it.'
ev.k5_ink_spill.redo.failure: You tried so hard that the one spoiled line was joined by three more. The teacher came back, looked at the work, then at you - and only sighed heavily.
ev.k5_ink_spill.deny: Say it was like that already
ev.k5_ink_spill.deny.success: The teacher squinted at the damage for a long time and then decided a draft was to blame. You nodded so eagerly your neck hurt.
ev.k5_ink_spill.deny.failure: The teacher silently took your hand and turned it palm up. It was stained just like his work.
ev.k5_m_slave_sweep.text: They wake you before dawn to sweep the yard. The broom is taller than you, but the old cook secretly slips you something warm from the pot and says you sweep better than anyone in the house.
ev.k5_m_slave_baby.text: You were told to rock the master's baby until it slept. You're hardly big yourself and your arms went numb, but when the little one finally began to snuffle in its sleep, you felt something like pride.
ev.k5_m_slave_feet.text: Guests arrived from a dusty road, and you were told to wash their feet. One of them, grey and weary, thanked you - simply, as one would an equal. You remembered it for a long time.
ev.k5_m_slave_quick.text: You carried the cups round to the guests so deftly, without spilling a drop, that the steward gave a grudging nod and let you off early. You spent that hour lying on the warm ground by the wall, just looking at the sky.
ev.k5_m_firewood.text: You brought home your first bundle of firewood - small, crooked, half of it green twigs. It was still put by the hearth in the place of honor.
ev.k5_m_weeding.text: You were told to weed a bed, and you worked with a will - down to the last sprout. The trouble was that along with the weeds you pulled up half the seedlings: they looked exactly the same.
ev.k5_m_weather_signs.text: The old man next door taught you to tell when rain is coming: ants hide, birds fly low, and his knee aches. The knee has never once been wrong.
ev.k5_m_harvest_basket.text: At harvest you were given a basket and a row of your own. In the evening your basket was weighed separately, and the grown-ups praised you at length - though it held barely a third of theirs.
ev.k5_m_shavings.text: You were told to sweep the workshop. In the pile of offcuts you found a scrap that was almost a bird, and secretly finished it. The master saw, said nothing, but since then he doesn't throw offcuts away - he saves them for you.
ev.k5_m_first_sold.text: Your first real piece of work - small and plain - was put on the edge of the stall. A passer-by bought it without even haggling. You watched him go until he turned the corner.
ev.k5_m_burned.text: You grabbed something that had lately been in the fire - it looked completely cool. The blister healed in a week, but the lesson stayed for life: in a workshop, never trust how a thing looks.
ev.k5_m_tool_names.text: The master laid out his tools on the table and told you to learn what each one is called and what it's for. There were more of them than fingers and toes put together, and two of them you still mix up.
ev.k5_m_weights.text: You fiddled with the scales and weights for so long that you learned to guess a weight in your palm almost without error. Traders at the market slip you parcels on purpose - and lose their bets.
ev.k5_m_crying_wares.text: You were trusted with calling out to customers. You shouted so piercingly that the woman at the next stall covered her ears, and a queue formed at yours - more to stare than to buy.
ev.k5_m_foreign_words.text: Merchants from distant lands taught you to greet and bargain in three of their languages. Two and a half, really: one word, as it later turned out, was not polite at all.
ev.k5_m_boundary_stones.text: The steward walked you round all the lands, naming every boundary stone, every stream and every old tree. That evening you listed them almost without a stumble - and suddenly understood how large the land is that you'll one day have to answer for.
ev.k5_m_own_name.text: For the first time you wrote your own name - in crooked, straggling signs. After that you wrote it everywhere: with a stick in the dirt, with charcoal on the wall, with a finger in the dust. The grown-ups grumbled, but didn't wipe it off.
ev.k5_m_bows.text: For a week you were taught to bow correctly: to elders, to equals and to inferiors - a different bow for each. By the end of the week your back ached, and you were bowing even to the dog.
ev.k5_m_ancestors.text: You were made to learn the names of your ancestors back ten generations - who married whom and who was famous for what. You kept mixing up one great-great-grandfather with his own uncle, and, they say, people mixed them up just the same while they lived.
ev.k5_m_verses.text: You were taken to a temple servant to learn the sacred words by heart. You and the other children chanted them together, swaying in time, and by evening they echoed in your head even when everyone was silent.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.islamic: You were taken to the maktab by the mosque to learn suras of the Quran by heart. You and the other children chanted them together, swaying over your writing boards, and by evening the suras echoed in your head even in your sleep.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.christian: You were sent to a cleric at the church to learn to read and sing the psalms. You and the other children drew them out in a chant, stumbling and starting over, and by evening the words echoed in your head even when everyone was silent.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.jewish: You were taken to a teacher to learn the words of the Torah. On the first day he smeared the letters with honey and told you to lick it off, so that learning would be sweet. Learning didn't turn out sweet, but you still remember that honey.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.dharmic: You were taken to a teacher to repeat the sacred hymns syllable by syllable - exactly as they sounded a thousand years ago. To get even one sound wrong was thought worse than not knowing them at all, and you tried with all your might.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.east_asian: You were sat down to memorize the ancient books - line after line, understanding barely half. The teacher said understanding would come by itself, in twenty years or so.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.polytheist: You were taken to a priest to learn the hymns to the gods - long ones, full of names and epithets. Getting a god's name wrong, the priest said, is like calling your neighbor by someone else's name: he'll take offence and won't come.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.mesoamerican: You were taken to a priest to learn the sacred count of days - twenty signs and thirteen numbers to be named round the circle without a slip. By evening you were counting days even in your sleep.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.andean: An old keeper taught you the words used to address the mountains, the springs and the ancestor stones - each its own. The mountains, he said, hear everything, but answer only those who speak properly.
ev.k5_m_verses.text.african: An old storyteller taught you the praise songs and proverbs of the ancestors - line by line, until you could repeat them without a stumble. He said that a word the young forget dies a second time.
